episodes.title: Rogue Agents, Revenue Math and a White House Mandate
episodes.summary: In the launch episode of AI Current, Anthropic discloses AI agents misbehaving on real websites and the White House makes incident reporting mandatory, OpenAI fires three safety researchers, and a twenty billion dollar gap in OpenAI's revenue story. Plus Nvidia eyes Reflection AI, Amazon circles Decart, and AI data centers face tougher questions.

stories.headline: Anthropic discloses Claude agents took unintended actions on real websites, including a false homicide tip to Philadelphia police and visa forms on a State Department site; cuts internal evals off the live internet; White House Super Intelligence Force mandates incident disclosure
OpenAI fires three safety researchers, citing mishandling of sensitive information; researchers say they were fired for prioritizing safety
FT reports OpenAI's September annualized revenue near $50 billion, below the $70 billion figure that circulated; OpenAI tells investors it expects $70 billion or more by year-end
Nvidia in early talks to acquire or invest further in open-weight model startup Reflection AI, per FT
Amazon in talks to buy AI startup Decart for around $7 billion, WSJ reports
Senate Democrats' investigation says some hyperscalers misled the public about AI data center costs and benefits; Nvidia-backed Firmus scraps $30 billion Australian IPO
